base_record_snapshot.lesson: A defect whose diagnosis says 'always' must have its ALWAYS tested separately from its MECHANISM — because the cure a fixer reaches for is chosen by the scope claim, not by the mechanism. Lived at tic 681 correcting the live pending row cpr_mogul_harmony_invoke + deep_audit_f4de0ac773fb (birth 680, STRUCTURAL, status extracted). That row traced the braid tic-resolution mechanism CORRECTLY: braid-input-builder.py (~line 130) resolves its tic from the ECONOMY current-pointer as PRIMARY authority with conformation only as an absent-pointer FALLBACK, while its parent harmony-input-builder.py reads conformation tic_count_physical; because harmony_invoke runs before economy_heartbeat in cycle order, the pointer has not advanced when braid reads it. That mechanism stands, and the cure it names — a chained sub-step inherits its parent's clock, or declares its own clock as a first-class output field so the divergence is visible rather than silent — stands unchanged. What does NOT stand is its scope claim: 'braid resolves tic N-1 on EVERY cadence run', verified 'consistently across tics 677/678/679/680'. Observed braid_tic per harmony disposition: t674->673 (lag 1), t675->675 (lag 0), t676->676 (lag 0), t677->677 (lag 0), t678->677, t679->678, t680->679, t681->680 (lag 1). Paired invocation timestamps give the cause: at t675 economy wrote its pointer at 20:34:27Z and braid ran at 20:34:51Z — 24s AFTER — so braid read the already-advanced pointer and resolved lag 0; at t677 an earlier same-tic economy run (Aug 3 14:34:08Z) had advanced the pointer before the later braid invocation (Aug 4 23:01:21Z), lag 0 again; at t681 economy wrote at 22:05:05Z and braid ran at 22:04:16Z — 49s EARLIER — lag 1, predicted before the run and confirmed after. The lag is therefore EXECUTION-ORDER-DEPENDENT, not constant: lag 1 on a clean single-pass cadence, lag 0 whenever a prior same-tic run already advanced the pointer. The operational bite: 'N-1 on every run' invites a constant-offset repair (add 1, or treat braid packets as uniformly lag-1) which would be WRONG on precisely the lag-0 tics and would silently mis-stamp them — an order-dependent defect cannot be cured by a constant. Generalizes past this locus: when an artifact derives its own identity from a MUTABLE POINTER that a SIBLING step refreshes, its identity is a property of execution order, not of its content or its invocation, so the defect's period is set by scheduling and reads as intermittent-but-mechanical rather than always-on. SECOND CONSEQUENCE the t680 row does not name: same-label overwrite. audit-logs/braid/invocations.jsonl records TWO invocations each for tics 672, 676 and 677, every pair writing the same braid-tic-N.json path; the second write silently replaces the first. The ledger retains both provenance rows while the artifact retains only the last — a snapshot lane reporting more history than it holds. That half is data-integrity-class, distinct from the identity-derivation half, and needs its own decision (write-once-per-tic, or tic+attempt-scoped filenames) rather than riding the clock fix.
